segments.dry: Reviewers with dry skin, including one with rosacea and one with hashimoto's-related dryness, mostly report the oil is hydrating and well tolerated, though one reviewer with dry, acne-prone skin says it triggered big, deep breakouts for both her and her husband.
segments.combination: The one reviewer who specifies oily combination skin on her face, with a more sensitive neck, reports the oil works well for both areas, tightening the look of her pores and softening fine lines a little.
segments.sensitive: A very large number of reviewers describe their skin as sensitive, extremely sensitive, or eczema-prone and report the oil is gentle with little to no irritation, redness or peeling even as first-time retinol users; one reviewer, without stating her own skin type, says it burned her skin immediately and disputes the sensitive-skin claim.
segments.mature: A reviewer with menopausal, dry, sensitive skin reports it calmed her irritation and left her skin more supple, a 49-year-old first-time retinol user reports zero reaction using it daily, and another reviewer calls it the best product for mature skin, describing her skin as soft, supple and radiant.

concerns.aging: Many reviewers, including several first-time retinol users, report softer or less noticeable fine lines within a few weeks of regular use, along with a firmer or brighter look to their skin; one reviewer says she is not yet sure whether it is having any anti-aging effect.
concerns.dehydration: Many reviewers, including several with dry skin, describe the oil as deeply hydrating, leaving their skin soft, moisturized and nourished rather than dry, with one reviewer specifically praising it for restoring skin dried out by sun exposure.
concerns.redness: Several reviewers report visibly reduced redness, including less noticeable redness on the cheeks and calmer rosacea-related skin; one reviewer with rosacea and dry skin instead describes only modest changes in tone and sensitivity after several weeks of use.
concerns.barrier: Multiple reviewers, including some with eczema-prone or very reactive skin, report no irritation, peeling or burning even as first-time retinol users, and a couple credit the formula's barrier lipids with supporting their skin barrier; by contrast, one reviewer says the serum burned her skin immediately despite the sensitive-skin claim.
concerns.blemishes: Most reviewers, including several who worried an oil-based formula would make them break out, report no new blemishes and some say their acne has improved; a minority describe the opposite, including two who report severe breakouts or deep pimples on the face and one who reports a rough purging period that left her skin looking worse than before starting.
concerns.spots: Several reviewers report fading of dark spots, sun spots or hyperpigmentation, along with a more even skin tone, after a few weeks of regular use.

extraits.titre: Not for my acne prone skin
extraits.texte: I tend to prefer to protect against my dry skin's tendency for acne with skin barrier and microbiome products and exfoliation, so I was willing to try an oil in this case, but unfortunately, it's not for my acne prone skin. Shortly after I started using it, I found I was breaking out with big, deep pimples in the areas that are most acne prone for me. My husband had the same experience. I was bummed because we really wanted to like it!

I like the product, overall. This is the first retinol product I've tried. I have rosacea, and started using this product every 2 nights for a few weeks. Then, moved to every other night for a few more weeks, before using it every night for the last several weeks. I also have dry skin. So, the oil formula is nice for me. I have noticed some modest changes in tone and sensitivity since starting this product. I removed a star when I read the answer to a customer-submitted question about the percentage (dose or strength) of retinol in the product. (I was searching for this answer, as well. I wanted to start researching what I could step up to next, which is normal for retinol use.)The answer provided by Byoma cited that it would be "giving away secrets" if they were to disclose this information. This is untrue. Many other companies list the strength of the retinol products right on the front of their packaging, and others on the back, or they provide it online. This is important information to have with retinol use. (Compare it to a company marketing a sunblock, but refusing to tell you the SPF, as it's a "secret".) I removed another star when I realized that this is just a ploy to get you to continue to use their product, because even though they market it as "beginner and sensitive-friendly," they don't give you the information you would need (the strength) to be able to make an informed decision about your skin after you've completed a cycle with this product, and are ready t

I received this product complimentary from BYOMA in exchange for my honest review. First time trying out BYOMA Sensitive Retinol Oil. I like that this oil is soothing upon application. The texture is a lightweight oil which is designed for sensitive skin and first-time retinol users. I appreciate its quick absorption and nourishing properties. I have oily combination skin but my neck is sensitive skin type. I am glad this retinol works well for both my face and neck. Even though it is an oil, I use just about 2 small drops and it seems enough for my skin. It doesn't make my face feel grasy. I see slight improvement, it appears to soften my fine lines a little bit, and my pores appear to be tighter. It is a gentle yet effective addition to my skincare routine!

I have extremely sensitive skin and this is the first retinol I have used that actually reduced skin irriatation. I've noticed improvement in my hyperpigmentation and keratosis after using it 3 nights a week for about 3 months. The oil is very light weight and has almost no scent. This would be a great retinol for a beginner. This is gentle enough that I think it could be used every night. I would apply a light weight moisturizer before the oil to avoid irriation.
